mathgap.title: Sequential processing of transfers
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately adjust both the giver's and receiver's counts. All subsequent statements must use these updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form "X gives K items to Y" is encountered.
mathgap.example: Ignoring the transfer and using the original counts for later comparisons.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: Translate statements that equate a signed difference to another difference as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says "the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of Y that C and D have".
mathgap.example: Treating the equality as |A - B| = |C - D|, losing sign information.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person (e.g., "X has N items"), set that person's current count to N at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement provides an explicit integer count for a person.
mathgap.example: Treating a later mention of the same person as a new unknown instead of using the given count.

mathgap.title: Update both parties in a transfer
mathgap.principle: For a transfer "X gives K items to Y", subtract K from X's current count and add K to Y's current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement is processed.
mathgap.example: Adding K only to the receiver while leaving the giver unchanged.

mathgap.title: Systematic linear solving
mathgap.principle: After translating all statements into algebraic equations, collect them into a linear system and solve for all unknowns, checking consistency.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After all statements have been parsed and expressed as equations.
mathgap.example: Attempting to guess values without solving the resulting linear system.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All item counts must be non‑negative integers; discard any solution that yields a negative or fractional count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the linear system, before finalizing the answer.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person ends up with -3 items.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For conditional transfers, first evaluate the condition using the current counts; only if the condition holds should the transfer be applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement includes a condition such as "If X has at least K items, then X gives K to Y".
mathgap.example: Applying the transfer unconditionally without checking the condition.

mathgap.title: Redistribution equalization handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two persons redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount, pool their items and split the total evenly.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a phrase like "X and Y redistribute their items equally".
mathgap.example: Leaving the original counts unchanged instead of equalizing them.

mathgap.title: Combined statements handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement contains multiple relational clauses (e.g., "X has N more than Y and M fewer than Z"), split it into separate equations for each clause.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a single sentence encodes more than one relationship.
mathgap.example: Treating the whole sentence as a single equation and missing one of the relationships.

mathgap.title: Signed interpretation of "difference between" phrase
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions "the difference between the number of X and Y", interpret it as the signed difference (X - Y) preserving the order of names, not as an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase like "difference between the number of A and B" appears, especially within equality-of-differences statements.
mathgap.example: Treating "difference between A and B" as |A - B|, which loses sign information and leads to incorrect equations.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase "difference between" is often interpreted as a magnitude, causing loss of sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two names and treat the expression as (first - second).

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Transfers are sometimes processed after all other statements, forgetting that later statements depend on updated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when encountered, before processing subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Direct count statements are taken as final values, overlooking later transfers that modify them.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as current values at that point; allow later transfers to change them.

mathgap.description: Updating only the receiver in a transfer
mathgap.why_it_happens: The giver's count is mistakenly left unchanged, violating conservation of items.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver.

mathgap.description: Reversing the direction in "X has N more than Y" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The inequality is misread, leading to X = Y - N instead of X = Y + N.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "X has N more than Y" as X = Y + N.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase is taken as an absolute difference rather than a signed one.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve order and treat it as (first - second).

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting "increase by N times" as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The wording suggests multiplication, but models may add instead.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "increase by N times" as multiplying the original count by N.
